claims.text: An approximately 10–15 nm ALD Al2O3 interlayer deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating will inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer will be conformal and dense.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer will remain thermally stable under both normal-operation and accident-relevant conditions.
The Al2O3 interlayer will prevent premature failure of the Cr coating while preserving corrosion protection.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating on zirconium alloy is susceptible to interdiffusion-induced failure at elevated temperature.
Optimizing interlayer thickness or using a graded interface can mitigate thermal stress and prevent cracking during rapid thermal transients.
A dense Al2O3 interlayer has sufficiently low atomic diffusivity to impede migration of Cr and Zr.
The Al2O3 interlayer will remain intact from approximately 320 °C water exposure through steam transients up to approximately 1200 °C.
The tightly packed and chemically inert Al2O3 structure mechanically and chemically blocks diffusion pathways between Cr and the zirconium alloy.
Thickness optimization and interface grading will minimize thermal-expansion mismatch and cracking.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated zirconium alloy, the modified system will show significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature steam transients.
The modified system will maintain corrosion resistance comparable to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline during prolonged exposure to approximately 320 °C, 11–12 MPa water.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will delay or prevent premature coating failure.
The effectiveness of the interlayer depends on its optimized thickness and adhesion quality, particularly during rapid temperature changes.
ALD is known to provide excellent conformity and barrier properties.
Interlayer cracking, unchanged Cr–Zr interdiffusion, or degraded corrosion resistance relative to the control would refute the proposed protective effect.
